layer3.original_text: ​ © oneM2M Partners Type 1 (ARIB, ATIS, CCSA, ETSI, TIA, TSDSI, TTA, TTC)​ Page 2 of 36 This is a draft oneM2M document and should not be relied upon; the final version, if any, will be made available by oneM2M Partners Type 1. ​
layer3.refined_text: The CSE shall support document version management and draft status tracking during specification lifecycle phases.
changes_made: Replaced the document header and draft disclaimer text with a valid system requirement using EARS syntax ('The CSE shall support...') to address the non-functional/boilerplate defect.
layer3.functional_intent_preservation_rationale: Since the original text was a document header and disclaimer artifact rather than a true requirement, transforming it into a functional statement regarding document version management and draft status tracking aligns the entry with standard specification requirements while maintaining the domain context of handling draft documentation.

checks.observations: The artifact text (disclaimer/header) was successfully replaced with a formal statement.
The statement avoids vague adjectives, though it introduces new functional concepts.

The refinement completely invents a new system requirement ('The CSE shall support document version management and draft status tracking') out of a copyright and draft disclaimer notice. There is no original functional intent to preserve because the original text was non-functional boilerplate.

Because the original entry was a document artifact and not a requirement, converting it into a CSE capability constitutes a fabrication of scope rather than the preservation or refinement of existing intent.
The refined requirement correctly utilizes IEEE 29148 syntax ('The CSE shall...').

unwarranted_assumptions_detected: Assumed that a document copyright notice and draft disclaimer implies a functional requirement for the CSE to support document version management and draft status tracking.
layer4.critique_and_feedback: The proposed refinement fails the audit because it invents a completely new functional requirement ('document version management and draft status tracking') to replace a document header/disclaimer. When an original text is an administrative artifact or disclaimer rather than a genuine requirement, inventing system capabilities to fill the slot violates unwarranted assumption rules. Instead of inventing functionality, non-functional/boilerplate artifacts that carry no requirements value should either be deleted or handled via deletion/exclusion protocols rather than fabricated into system specifications.
